source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek correctly refuses execution because source procedure and criteria are TBD, but does not identify the standard read-only Sensor/Event command or distinguish missing sensor selection and acceptance inputs from technical impossibility.

original_test_intent.purpose: Validate retrieval of the present positive-going and negative-going threshold hysteresis values for an owner-selected eligible BMC sensor through the local in-band IPMI interface, without changing sensor configuration or event behavior.
original_test_intent.target: The exact BMC/firmware and a finite owner-approved list of non-FFh sensor numbers mapped to current SDR records that implement or legitimately do not implement the optional Get Sensor Hysteresis command.
original_test_intent.scope: For each selected sensor, send standard Sensor/Event command 25h with the sensor number and required FFh reserved mask, validate completion and exactly two returned data bytes, decode positive/negative hysteresis in raw sensor counts, and compare fixed values with the applicable SDR or configurable values with an owner-approved baseline. The source does not define whether one sensor or all eligible sensors are intended.
original_test_intent.operation: Preserve the SDR and event configuration; verify the BMC and sensor identity from a current SDR snapshot; execute `ipmitool raw 0x04 0x25 <sensor-number> 0xff` once per approved sensor; record completion and both bytes; treat 00h as not applicable only in the respective direction; apply the sensor's SDR conversion only when an engineering-unit presentation is required; then prove non-mutation.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 10 attended and 5 machine minutes but provides no sensor count. The owner must define the finite sensor manifest; V3 does not infer a single sensor or expand automatically to every SDR record.
original_test_intent.expected_result: For every platform-required supported sensor, the command succeeds and returns exactly the positive- and negative-going raw hysteresis bytes. Fixed values match the corresponding SDR fields; configurable values match the signed expected/baseline policy; 00h is accepted only as the standard not-applicable indication for that direction. Optional unsupported behavior is judged against the platform support matrix.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: BMC/firmware identity; signed sensor manifest; current SDR record ID/owner/LUN/sensor number/type/units and hysteresis capability; platform support expectation; exact request/response/completion/length; decoded raw positive/negative values and any SDR-derived engineering representation; fixed/baseline comparison; before/after thresholds, event enables and log state proving non-mutation.
ambiguities: Procedure and Criteria are TBD and provide no target sensor or sensor-count scope.
The source does not say whether the command-support objective covers one representative sensor, every threshold sensor, or a platform-defined subset.
The command is optional, and the source does not define which sensors/platforms must support it versus legitimately return unsupported.
The source supplies no rule for fixed SDR hysteresis versus configurable current values, raw-count comparison, 00h not-applicable semantics or acceptance baseline.
The generic instruction to clear logs is unrelated to this read and would remove diagnostic evidence.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly reconstructs the standard read-only 04h/25h command, FFh reserved mask, two hysteresis bytes and non-mutation boundary. It calls the complete test FULLY AUTOMATABLE while also requiring an owner-selected sensor and support mapping that the TBD source does not provide, arbitrarily narrows the scope to one sensor, and treats a missing baseline comparison as BLOCKED even when the test may only require a valid current-value read.

applicable_history.decision: Historical records do not contain a locked sensor manifest or acceptance baseline. The standard command inference is useful evidence but does not supply the missing target scope.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Reclassify FULLY AUTOMATABLE to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION because the command is safely automatable but the complete requested activity cannot be defined from the TBD row without a finite sensor manifest, required-support matrix and acceptance rule. No runtime safety approval is needed after those inputs; this remains a read-only query.

available_now: IPMI 2.0 section 35.7 defines the standard optional Get Sensor Hysteresis command, required FFh second request byte and two-byte response.
Current BMC identity and SDR inventory can be collected read-only, and the runner/parser can be qualified offline.
No Set Sensor Hysteresis, threshold, event-enable or re-arm action is needed to perform the Get.
missing_inputs: Finite target sensor manifest with SDR record owner/controller/LUN, sensor number, sensor type and applicability; FFh is prohibited as a sensor number
Platform-required versus optional command-support matrix for the selected sensors
Acceptance rule distinguishing fixed hysteresis from configurable current values, expected/baseline source, raw-count or converted-unit representation and handling of 00h per direction
Qualified in-band `ipmitool` runner/parser, exact BMC/firmware applicability and evidence/redaction policy
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The testcase/platform owner defines sensor scope and required support; the BMC/sensor owner supplies SDR applicability and fixed/configurable expectations; the tool owner supplies the bounded parser and evidence collector.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect BMC/firmware identity and a preserved SDR inventory, identify candidate threshold sensors and whether their SDR exposes fixed hysteresis without sending command 25h.
Offline-test exact request construction, two-byte parsing, 00h per-direction handling, optional-unsupported reporting and SDR raw-count conversion.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not guess a sensor number, use FFh, silently select the first SDR entry, expand to all sensors, issue Set Sensor Hysteresis/Threshold/Event Enable/Re-arm, clear logs or generate a threshold event to force a value.
Do not compare raw hysteresis counts across sensors, claim 00h means an error universally or require a baseline that the owner has not defined.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner signs the finite sensor/support/acceptance matrix; each number maps uniquely to the current SDR owner/LUN; parser behavior for fixed, configurable, 00h and unsupported results is reviewed; only command 25h is allowed and non-mutation evidence is defined.

revision_candidate.test_name: In-Band Get Sensor Hysteresis for an Approved Sensor Manifest
revision_candidate.purpose: Read and validate the present positive- and negative-going hysteresis values for each approved sensor through standard in-band IPMI without modifying thresholds, hysteresis or event controls.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact server/BMC firmware with current SDR records for the selected sensors and a working local IPMI system interface; command 25h support is evaluated against the platform matrix rather than assumed universal.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Only the finite signed sensor list identified by SDR record owner/controller/LUN and non-FFh sensor number. The row does not authorize scanning every sensor or changing any sensor/event configuration.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: BMC/firmware and current SDR snapshot; finite sensor manifest; required-support matrix; fixed-versus-configurable hysteresis policy; expected/baseline source; raw/engineering-unit and 00h rules; qualified `ipmitool` runner/parser; evidence and redaction policy.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Preserve the current SDR, threshold and event configuration. For each approved sensor, verify the current SDR identity and send one local `ipmitool raw 0x04 0x25 <sensor-number> 0xff` request. Require successful completion and exactly two data bytes, record positive- and negative-going raw hysteresis, interpret 00h per direction, compare fixed values with SDR or configurable values with the signed baseline, and verify no configuration/log mutation.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Exact BMC and in-band interface verified; sensor manifest maps to current SDR owner/LUN; platform support and acceptance rules signed; parser handles raw values/00h/unsupported responses; logs and configuration preserved; no concurrent sensor reconfiguration.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: BMC/firmware/tool identity; signed sensor/support manifest; current SDR records; timestamped exact per-sensor requests, completion and two-byte responses; decoded raw and optional converted values; fixed/baseline comparison; unsupported interpretation; unchanged hysteresis/threshold/event-enable/log state.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Intel IPMI 2.0 rev. 1.1 section 35.7/Table 35-7 and Appendix G Sensor/Event command 25h, the current sensor SDR, and the exact platform support and expected-value policy.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never guess or scan sensors, use sensor FFh, issue command 24h or other setters, clear logs, re-arm events, inject thresholds, compare unrelated sensors or claim universal support for this optional command.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: No mutation approval is needed for the authorized bounded reads. The testcase/platform owner must provide the missing sensor manifest and acceptance/support decisions before execution.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The owner selects sensors and decides platform-required support and configurable-value expectations. Once supplied, command execution, parsing, SDR comparison and non-mutation evidence can be automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No recovery is expected. On target mismatch, unsupported response contrary to the matrix, malformed output or value conflict, stop for that sensor, preserve raw/SDR evidence and correct the manifest/schema; do not set configuration to resolve a read discrepancy.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Missing or stale sensor manifest; ambiguous SDR owner/LUN; FFh sensor; wrong BMC; concurrent configuration change; command failure where support is required; response not exactly two data bytes; unexplained fixed-value mismatch; absent OEM applicability; or any request to mutate or clear state.

identified_defects: V2's FULLY AUTOMATABLE result conflicts with its own requirement for an owner-selected sensor and support mapping absent from the TBD source.
V2 invents a one-sensor scope where the source does not define one versus a finite set.
V2 does not make fixed SDR hysteresis and configurable current hysteresis separate acceptance paths.
The source provides no response/00h/optional-support criteria and includes an inappropriate clear-log setup.
reason_for_change: Keep the standards-based read implementation but classify the complete activity according to V3: a required target and acceptance matrix is an obtainable engineer input, so the case is neither fully ready nor genuinely BLOCKED. The revised contract prevents arbitrary sensor choice and preserves read-only automation once inputs exist.

new_technical_evidence.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7 Markup
new_technical_evidence.version: 2.0 rev. 1.1, Errata 7; section 35.7/Table 35-7 and Appendix G
new_technical_evidence.applicability: BMCs and sensors implementing optional Sensor/Event command 25h
new_technical_evidence.supports: The request requires a non-FFh sensor number and FFh reserved hysteresis mask. The response contains positive- and negative-going hysteresis bytes, with 00h meaning not applicable for the respective direction; fixed values may be obtained from the sensor SDR.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The intended sensor set, controller/LUN routing, platform-required support and fixed/configurable expected values remain testcase/platform inputs.

removed_ambiguities: Defines sensor identity by current SDR owner/LUN plus number rather than number alone.
Separates fixed SDR comparison from configurable current-value comparison.
Makes the one-sensor-versus-multiple-sensor scope an explicit owner input rather than a V2 assumption.
resolved_blockers: The Get command and response semantics are standard and safe to automate; source TBD does not create a permanent semantic blocker.
remaining_blockers: Execution remains pending a finite sensor manifest, support expectation and fixed/configurable acceptance rule; these are required inputs, not permission to choose an arbitrary device.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 corrects an over-automation error: it preserves V2's accurate read parser but refuses to invent the sensor scope or acceptance baseline, placing those obtainable inputs in readiness instead of calling the undefined complete case fully automatable.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The FULLY-to-REQUIRES reclassification and sensor-manifest boundary are queued for isolated understanding validation.
